assumptions: The exception 'Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal' is omitted because that direction cannot be seen or expressed in the DSL; the rule is applied as if no such direction was given.
The presence of a stop sign and an intersection is not checked; the provided 'inspection' zone and 'packing_entry' line are assumed to be positioned at that stop sign and intersection.
The tracked object is the vehicle; the driver's stopping behaviour is represented by the vehicle's motion.

The anchor is 'bottom_center' because the waiting zone and stop line are on the road surface and this is the vehicle's ground-contact point, whereas 'center' would cross road markings earlier in projection.
A stop is interpreted as a DWELL in 'inspection', the waiting zone just before the stop line, while still at a maximum speed of 0.05 for at least 1000 ms.

Approaching traffic is assumed to cross 'packing_entry' in the 'to_right' direction, corresponding to travelling from top to bottom of the frame as described for that line; crossings in the opposite direction do not trigger this rule.
No time limit is placed on the interval between stopping and crossing, so BEFORE uses within_ms null (unbounded), as the statute states no such limit.
Vehicles that never cross 'packing_entry' pass the rule, following the IMPLIES(OCCURS(B), BEFORE(A, B)) idiom; stopping outside 'inspection' does not count as stopping at the stop line.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: Every approaching vehicle that crosses the stop line must first dwell, stopped, in the inspection zone before that crossing.

provenance.reason: Tracked object is the vehicle itself.

provenance.reason: bottom_center (ground contact/wheels) is the point that aligns with the ground-drawn stop line and waiting zone described in the zone/line definitions, rather than the center of the bounding box.
'inspection' is defined as the waiting zone in the approach lanes just before the stop line, matching the statute's stopping location.

provenance.quote: at a clearly marked stop line
provenance.reason: 'packing_entry' is defined as the stop line across the approach lanes.
Per line definition, cars approaching travel top to bottom of frame, and moving downwards across the line = to_right.
DWELL with max_speed threshold operationalises 'stop' in the zone before the line.
Statute requires a stop but specifies no minimum duration; 1000 ms is a conventional minimum dwell to distinguish a genuine stop from momentary slowing, assumed for measurability.
Statute requires the vehicle to stop but gives no numeric speed; 0.05 is the DSL's stated threshold for stopped/still.
Statute requires stopping before proceeding past the line but specifies no maximum gap between stop and crossing; null = unbounded.

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
